items.title: United States (Diplomatic focus on Iran), United States: Pakistan's foreign minister and Saudi Arabia's foreign minister confirmed in a phone call that an electronic signing ceremony for a U.S.-Iran deal is scheduled for June 14, indicating the negotiations have reached a final stage.
items.description: Pakistan's foreign minister and Saudi Arabia's foreign minister confirmed in a phone call that an electronic signing ceremony for a U.S.-Iran deal is scheduled for June 14, indicating the negotiations have reached a final stage.
items.rawSummary: A planned electronic signing ceremony for a U.S.-Iran nuclear deal was announced by Pakistani and Saudi officials while President Trump denounced Iran's version of the terms as inaccurate.
items.analysis: The U.S.-Iran diplomatic push remains volatile after Iran released its version of a tentative agreement, drawing sharp rebukes from President Trump, who called the published terms inaccurate and accused Iranian leaders of bad-faith negotiations. U.S. officials outlined stringent conditions—including destroying nuclear materials, dismantling the program, permanently opening the Strait of Hormuz, and halting terror funding—with no sanctions relief until compliance is verified. Amid the confusion, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif claimed a deal was near, and now Pakistan's foreign minister and Saudi Arabia's foreign minister have confirmed that an electronic signing ceremony is scheduled for tomorrow, signaling that talks have reached a final stage; U.S. officials have not publicly commented on the ceremony. Meanwhile, U.S. military planning included a pause on a ground mission to seize Iran's highly enriched uranium and ongoing contingency discussions about deploying Department of Energy specialists if a deal is reached, while Trump spoke with Netanyahu to stress that Iranian compliance must precede any sanctions relief. Separately, outgoing DNI Tulsi Gabbard declassified evidence of a U.S.-funded biological laboratory program in over 30 countries, including Ukraine.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz area (Bandar Abbas vicinity), Iran: U.S. A-10 aircraft have reportedly destroyed two Iranian speedboats, as shown by kill markings, while carrying a range of munitions for air-to-ground and anti-drone operations.
items.description: U.S. A-10 aircraft have reportedly destroyed two Iranian speedboats, as shown by kill markings, while carrying a range of munitions for air-to-ground and anti-drone operations.
items.rawSummary: Amid stalled nuclear negotiations, Iran and the U.S. have clashed in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian drone attacks on commercial ships, U.S. interceptions, and reported U.S. airstrikes destroying Iranian speedboats, while maritime traffic continues under heavy escort.
items.analysis: The standoff over the Strait of Hormuz intensified further as U.S. A-10 aircraft reportedly destroyed two Iranian speedboats, based on kill markings, indicating direct American strikes beyond the defensive drone interceptions announced earlier. This escalation followed an overnight Iranian drone attack on commercial vessels, all of which were downed by U.S. forces according to CENTCOM. The military actions unfold as diplomatic contacts remain deadlocked, with President Trump rejecting leaked Iranian terms and demanding nuclear dismantlement before any funds are released. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi simultaneously declared the strait under Iranian and Omani sovereignty and announced mandatory service fees, clarifying they are not tolls under international law. Despite the aggressive rhetoric and exchanges of fire, maritime traffic continues to flow unimpeded, and roughly 7 million barrels per day of non-Iranian oil still exit the Persian Gulf under U.S. military escort. Persistent internal fissures among Iranian leaders, particularly between IRGC factions seeking maximalist concessions and other officials disputing a leaked draft memorandum, further complicate the prospects for a negotiated settlement.

items.rawSummary: Nuclear negotiations with the US remain unresolved amid internal Iranian disagreements, while Iran has sealed off its enriched uranium stockpile, is contending with widening banking disruptions, and is preparing funeral ceremonies for Supreme Leader Khamenei.
items.analysis: Persistent internal disagreements remain among Iranian leaders over nuclear concessions, with IRGC commander Major General Ahmad Vahidi's circle reportedly seeking an agreement tantamount to US surrender, while other officials disputed a leaked draft. Conflicting US and Iranian accounts suggest core issues remain unresolved. Foreign Minister Araghchi acknowledged both supporters and opponents within the Council, stated a collective decision is pending, and noted a possible remote signing within days, though he warned Iran will not proceed to a second phase without full implementation of the first. CNN reported that Iran has sealed off parts of its highly enriched uranium stockpile by collapsing tunnel entrances and placing mines, making the material harder to reach and potentially complicating any future deal to remove or destroy it. On the domestic front, extensive funeral ceremonies were announced for Khamenei, with processions in Tehran and Qom leading to a July 9 burial at Imam Reza Shrine, while Fars news agency reported a disruption of electronic banking services at four major banks early on June 13, possibly a cyberattack, and later the outages expanded to affect additional banks, with officials yet to confirm the cause.
